predecessors.name: Seleucid Empire
predecessors.text: the Seleucid satrapy of Commagene: 'the local satrap, Ptolemaeus of Commagene, established himself as an independent ruler' after Antiochus IV Epiphanes died (about 163 BC; the text elsewhere says…

successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: 'Emperor Vespasian deposed the dynasty and definitively re-annexed the territory to the Roman Empire' in 72 (province of Syria)

ledger.x: 163 BC: the Seleucid satrap Ptolemaeus makes Commagene independent.
64 BC: Antiochus I as Pompey's ally.
27 BC: the republic's relation passes to the Empire.
27 BC: Commagene a client of the Roman Empire.
17: Tiberius annexes Commagene ('Emperor Tiberius annexed Commagene to the province of Syria') and the client status ends; the loss event follows.
38: Caligula reinstates Antiochus IV and gives back Commagene.
38: Caligula adds a strip of coastal Cilicia. received a strip of coastal Cilicia.
About 40 (bridged): the client status lapses with the deposition (see the 40 loss).
41 (bridged): the Cilician strip returns with the kingdom.
41: client status resumes with the restoration.
72: the client status ends with Vespasian's annexation ('deposed the dynasty and definitively re-annexed the territory to the Roman Empire').
72: Vespasian deposes the dynasty and Commagene goes to Rome.
72: the Cilician strip goes with Commagene.

wars.name: Third Mithridatic War
wars.outcome: No land changed: 'Antiochus was an ally of the Roman general Pompey during the latter's campaigns against Mithridates VI of Pontus in 64 BC' and 'was able to keep Commagene independent from the Romans'.

wars.name: Roman-Parthian War of 58-63
wars.outcome: No Commagenian land is recorded as changing hands.

wars.name: Roman annexation of Commagene
wars.outcome: Antiochus IV deposed on the governor's charge of conspiring with the Parthians; his sons fled to Parthia after a brief clash; Commagene joined the province of Syria.

certainty.note: The Euphrates and the Taurus bound the kingdom but no page gives a treaty or survey line; the 17-38 gap and the Cilician strip are approximate.
